translationRepairs: The Grand Preceptor knew how to command men, and his rewards and punishments matched every deed.

太尉 is Grand Commandant, Li Guangbi's office; "Grand Preceptor" mistranslates it.
大父 means grandfather, not great-grandfather.

Gao Gu was descended from the High Ancestor Kan, who in the Yonghui era served as Beiting pacification commissioner, captured the Chebi qaghan alive, and rose to Protector-General of the Pacified East, as recorded in earlier annals.

Gao Gu was the great-great-grandson of Gao Kan, who in the Yonghui era served as Beiting pacification commissioner, captured the Chebi qaghan alive, and rose to Protector-General of the Pacified East, as recorded in earlier annals.
高祖 here means great-great-grandfather, not "High Ancestor".
The qaghan ordered his people: "Whoever takes Hao Ci alive shall receive a reward in gold equal to his height."
The Tibetan tsenpo ordered his people: "Whoever takes Hao Ci alive shall receive a reward in gold equal to his height."
贊普 is the Tibetan tsenpo, not a qaghan.

In his thirteenth year of service he became acting Left Regular Attendant, prefect of Weizhou, and Censor-in-Chief, with command of the Jingyuan campaign army and overall military authority at Pingliang, and was enfeoffed as Prince of Baoding.

In the thirteenth year (of Yuanhe) he became acting Left Regular Attendant, prefect of Weizhou, and Censor-in-Chief, with command of the Jingyuan campaign army and overall military authority at Pingliang, and was enfeoffed as Prince of Baoding.
十三年 continues the Yuanhe dating (818), not years of service.
